title: Hazel and the Veil
premise: Emrys Galloway keeps a sealed gate between realms and sells harmless charms in Greyhollow, a city that outlawed magic after the Sundering. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, Emrys meets Hazel Thorne, a hedge-witch who slipped through the failing veil carrying half of a broken covenant-stone. Hunted by the Wardens' Guild and shadowed by creatures starving on the other side of the veil, they must reunite the stone's halves at the gate before the moon's thirteenth turn seals both realms into slow death. In the end, Emrys must choose between restoring the covenant — which demands a keeper be bound to the gate forever — or letting Hazel take their place; instead they shatter the old law entirely, sharing the binding so neither is alone, and the stars return.
about_author: Cyrus Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore along old trade routes. They write quiet, aching fantasy about people who keep doors that others would rather forget exist.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In Greyhollow, Emrys sells a luck-charm to a frightened child while hiding the truth of their keeper's oath. At midnight the wards fail and every star vanishes at once. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine — the life Emrys built is already over, and they don't know it yet.

chapters.title: A Stranger Through the Hedge
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel stumbles out of a tearing veil into an alley, clutching half of a cracked covenant-stone, pursued by something with too many joints. Emrys finds her before the Wardens do. Emotional beat: wary recognition — two keepers of secrets recognizing each other instantly.

chapters.title: What the Guild Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Warden-Captain Ilsa Vane interrogates the neighborhood; Emrys lies badly and hides Hazel in the cellar beneath the charm shop. Flashback reveals the Sundering and why magic was outlawed. Emotional beat: guilt — Emrys realizes their three years of silence helped build this hunt.

chapters.title: The Half That Sings
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The stone-half hums with her family's voices from beyond the veil; she confesses she stole it fleeing a realm already dying of starlessness. Emrys admits the gate under the city is real — and theirs to guard. Emotional beat: trust kindling through shared confession.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. An old covenant-ghost explains the deadline: when the moon completes its thirteenth turn, the veil hardens permanently and both realms suffocate. The second stone-half lies in the Guild's vault. Emotional beat: the clock starts — fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Vane raids the shop; Emrys burns it deliberately to erase evidence, losing everything they spent three years building. The pair flee into the undercity with a Warden defector, Tam. Emotional beat: grief for the small safe life — and liberation in having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Vault of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Infiltrating the Guild vault, they find the second stone-half — and learn Vane wants the covenant reforged too, but with the Guild holding the gate as a weapon. A fight costs Tam his freedom. Emotional beat: betrayal of purpose — even allies want to own the door.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Gate
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the buried gate, the halves refuse to join: the covenant demands one willing keeper bound forever. Hazel offers herself; Emrys refuses and offers themself. Their argument becomes a confession of love neither planned. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. As the moon completes its turn, Emrys and Hazel seize the stone together and break the covenant's single-keeper clause, forging a shared binding just as the veil begins to seal. Vane, arriving to claim the gate, chooses at last to stand aside. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice transformed into partnership.

chapters.title: Two Keepers, One Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The stars return over both realms; the veil stands open but guarded, trade and letters crossing carefully. Emrys rebuilds not a hidden shop but a doorway-house where Hazel's family visits. Emotional beat: belonging — the price of survival paid jointly, and found family on both sides of the door.
